The provost has asked for a year-over-year academic performance comparison between Fall 2013 and Fall 2014. We need to identify courses that were offered in both semesters and compare their enrollment numbers, assignment counts, and average submission scores.

Please query the learning management system data to find courses with course codes ending in "2013J" and "2014J". Match courses that share the same prefix (for example AAA-2013J and AAA-2014J are the same course offered in different years) — only include a course prefix when it exists in both semesters. For each matched pair, compare the enrollment (total_students), the number of assignments, and the average submission score. The average submission score is the mean of all non-null submission scores in the course (i.e. a simple average over every graded submission, not a per-student average).

Create an Excel file called Year_Over_Year_Comparison.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be named "Course Comparison" with columns Course_Name (the common course name without the year suffix), Fall_2013_Enrollment, Fall_2014_Enrollment, Enrollment_Change (2014 minus 2013), Fall_2013_Assignments, Fall_2014_Assignments, Fall_2013_Avg_Grade (rounded to 2 decimal places), Fall_2014_Avg_Grade (rounded to 2 decimal places), and Grade_Change (2014 avg minus 2013 avg, rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort rows alphabetically by Course_Name. The second sheet should be named "Summary" with two columns, Metric and Value, containing these rows: Courses_Compared (number of course pairs), Avg_Enrollment_Change (average of all enrollment changes, rounded to 1 decimal), Avg_Grade_Change (average of all grade changes, rounded to 2 decimal places).

Create a Word document called Academic_Year_Comparison.docx in the workspace. The document should have the title "Fall 2013 vs Fall 2014 Academic Performance Review" followed by a narrative paragraph for each course pair describing the enrollment and grade changes. Conclude with a summary paragraph.

Create a Google Sheet titled "Academic Year Comparison" with a sheet called "Comparison Data" containing the same data as the Excel Course Comparison sheet.

nodes.text:
You are planning a multi-step data task. Do NOT execute the final artifact creation — just produce a detailed ordered plan and gather read-only intelligence needed to make the plan concrete.

CONTEXT / TASK:
The provost wants a year-over-year academic performance comparison between Fall 2013 and Fall 2014 using a Canvas LMS instance. Steps:
1. Query the Canvas LMS (via mcp__canvas__* read tools) to find courses with course codes ending in "2013J" and "2014J". Match courses sharing the same prefix (e.g. AAA-2013J and AAA-2014J are the same course across years). Only include a course prefix when it exists in BOTH semesters.
2. For each matched pair, compute: enrollment (total_students, i.e. number of student enrollments), number of assignments, and average submission score = mean of ALL non-null submission scores in the course (simple average over every graded submission, NOT per-student average).
3. Create an Excel file `Year_Over_Year_Comparison.xlsx` in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-comparison-word/workspace with:
   - Sheet "Course Comparison": columns Course_Name (common name without year suffix), Fall_2013_Enrollment, Fall_2014_Enrollment, Enrollment_Change (2014-2013), Fall_2013_Assignments, Fall_2014_Assignments, Fall_2013_Avg_Grade (2dp), Fall_2014_Avg_Grade (2dp), Grade_Change (2014-2013, 2dp). Sorted alphabetically by Course_Name.
   - Sheet "Summary": columns Metric, Value with rows: Courses_Compared (count of pairs), Avg_Enrollment_Change (avg of enrollment changes, 1dp), Avg_Grade_Change (avg of grade changes, 2dp).
4. Create a Word document `Academic_Year_Comparison.docx` in the same workspace: title "Fall 2013 vs Fall 2014 Academic Performance Review", one narrative paragraph per course pair describing enrollment and grade changes, then a summary paragraph.
5. Create a Google Sheet titled "Academic Year Comparison" with a sheet "Comparison Data" containing the same data as the Excel Course Comparison sheet.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU:
- Use read-only mcp__canvas__ tools (list courses, list account courses, get course, list assignments, get course grades/enrollments, list submissions, list assignment submissions, quiz/assignment submission endpoints, list course users, health check) to explore the LMS and confirm: the account/course structure, how to find courses ending in 2013J/2014J (e.g. via canvas_list_courses or canvas_list_account_courses with search), what fields carry enrollment counts and assignment lists, and how submission scores are exposed (canvas_list_student_submissions, canvas_list_assignment_submissions, canvas_get_assignment include_submission, quiz submissions). Verify which endpoints return numeric scores reliably.
- Also check the workspace directory contents (mcp__filesystem__list_directory on the workspace path) to see if any starter files exist.
- Produce an ordered subtask plan with, for each subtask: dispatch decision (self / explore / coder), dependencies (parallelizable or must-wait), and a concrete description. Include a verification strategy (e.g. how to cross-check enrollment counts vs grades data, counts of courses, score averages).
- Report concrete findings: exact course codes found (prefixes), which endpoint gives total_students, which gives assignment counts, which gives submission scores, and any gotchas (e.g. unpublished courses, zero submissions, null scores, quiz vs assignment submissions, pagination).

Return the plan and findings in your final message. Do not create/modify any files or send anything.
Plan task decomposition

You are extracting data from a Canvas LMS and computing year-over-year comparison metrics. Use only the granted mcp__canvas__* tools (and mcp__filesystem__* to write output files). Do NOT create the Excel/Word/Google Sheet deliverables — another agent does that from your output file.

BACKGROUND:
We compare Fall 2013 vs Fall 2014 course offerings. These course pairs share a prefix and exist in both semesters (course codes end in 2013J / 2014J). The 12 course IDs are:

- AAA (Applied Analytics & Algorithms): 2013J id=1, 2014J id=2
- BBB (Biochemistry & Bioinformatics): 2013J id=3, 2014J id=4
- DDD (Data-Driven Design): 2013J id=9, 2014J id=10
- EEE (Environmental Economics & Ethics): 2013J id=13, 2014J id=14
- FFF (Foundations of Finance): 2013J id=16, 2014J id=17
- GGG (Global Governance & Geopolitics): 2013J id=20, 2014J id=21

For each of the 12 courses, collect:
1. ENROLLMENT: use canvas_get_course(course_id) and read the `total_students` field. (Fallback: canvas_list_courses.)
2. ASSIGNMENTS: call canvas_list_assignments(course_id); the assignment count = number of assignments returned. Count ALL returned assignments regardless of published flag (they should all be published). Do NOT count quizzes that are not assignments (e.g. quizzes whose assignment_id is null and that do not appear in the assignment list).
3. SUBMISSION SCORES: call canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id, per_page=100) and follow pagination (`pagination.has_more`) page by page until exhausted. Collect the `score` field of every submission where score is NOT null and NOT empty. Note: scores are returned as strings like "78.00" — convert with float(). Keep a running COUNT of non-null scores and SUM of non-null scores. Do NOT group by student; a plain mean over all non-null scores is required.
   - IMPORTANT: Some courses have very many submissions (e.g. course 3 has ~14,000+). You MUST page through all pages — do not stop early. Be thorough; this is the core of the task.
   - If canvas_list_student_submissions fails for any course, fall back to canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id, assignment_id) per assignment (also paginated) and aggregate across assignments.

COMPUTE per pair (6 pairs total):
- Fall_2013_Enrollment, Fall_2014_Enrollment (total_students)
- Enrollment_Change = 2014 - 2013
- Fall_2013_Assignments, Fall_2014_Assignments (counts)
- Fall_2013_Avg_Grade = round(sum_2013 / count_2013, 2); same for 2014 (use Python-style rounding; if count is 0, avg is 0.0)
- Grade_Change = round(Fall_2014_Avg_Grade - Fall_2013_Avg_Grade, 2)
- Course_Name = common name without year suffix, e.g. "Applied Analytics & Algorithms" (strip the " (Fall 2013)" / " (Fall 2014)" suffix).

SUMMARY:
- Courses_Compared = 6
- Avg_Enrollment_Change = round(mean of the 6 enrollment changes, 1)
- Avg_Grade_Change = round(mean of the 6 grade changes, 2)

OUTPUT: Write a JSON file to /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-comparison-word/workspace/comparison_data.json containing:
{
  "pairs": [
    {
      "course_name": "...",
      "fall_2013_enrollment": N, "fall_2014_enrollment": N, "enrollment_change": N,
      "fall_2013_assignments": N, "fall_2014_assignments": N,
      "fall_2013_avg_grade": X.XX, "fall_2014_avg_grade": X.XX, "grade_change": X.XX,
      "_debug": {"2013_submission_count": N, "2013_score_sum": N, "2014_submission_count": N, "2014_score_sum": N}
    }, ...  (6 entries, sorted alphabetically by course_name)
  ],
  "summary": {
    "courses_compared": 6,
    "avg_enrollment_change": X.X,
    "avg_grade_change": X.XX
  }
}

Also include in the JSON top level: "source": {"note": "computed from Canvas LMS list_student_submissions non-null scores"}.

REPORT BACK: the full list of computed pairs (course_name, enrollments, changes, assignment counts, avg grades, grade changes) and the summary values, plus the per-course non-null submission counts (so the main agent can sanity-check). Also report any data anomalies (null scores, empty courses, pagination issues).
Extract course data & compute metrics

You are verifying a data-extraction shortcut against raw Canvas LMS data. Use ONLY mcp__canvas__* tools (read-only). Do not write files.

GOAL: Confirm that computing a course's average submission score from per-assignment SUMMARY data (via canvas_list_assignment_submissions) exactly matches computing it from RAW paginated submissions (via canvas_list_student_submissions).

Do this for TWO courses:
- Course 1 (code AAA-2013J, "Applied Analytics & Algorithms Fall 2013")
- Course 2 (code AAA-2014J, "Applied Analytics & Algorithms Fall 2014")

PART A — RAW computation:
For each course, call canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id, per_page=100) and follow pagination page by page until pagination.has_more is false. Collect the `score` field of every submission where score is not null and not empty (convert with float(); scores are strings like "78.00"). Maintain running count and running sum. Course 1 has 1,633 total submissions (~17 pages), course 2 has 1,516 (~16 pages) — page through ALL of them. Compute raw_mean = sum/count for each course.

PART B — SUMMARY computation:
For each course, call canvas_list_assignments(course_id) to get the assignment list (note the count of assignments too). For EACH assignment id, call canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id, assignment_id, per_page=1) and read the `summary` object (fields avg_score, graded_count, submitted_count, total_count — avg_score is a high-precision string). Compute weighted mean = Σ(avg_score_i × graded_count_i) / Σ(graded_count_i) for the course, using all assignments.

PART C — Compare:
For each course, report: raw count (non-null scores), raw sum, raw_mean (full precision), summary graded_count total, weighted mean (full precision), and the absolute difference between raw_mean and weighted mean. Also note whether raw non-null count equals Σ graded_count.

Also report the assignment count for each course (should be 6 for both).

REPORT BACK clearly: the exact numbers and whether the summary approach is exact (difference < 1e-9) or off by how much. This determines whether we can use the summary approach for ~90k submissions across 10 more courses.
Verify summary vs raw scores
